why: The prompt names three concrete rooms - skeleton mobs, a pressure-plate gate puzzle, and a boss arena - with no stats, leveling, loot or quests, so 'action + puzzle' covers both halves while 'rpg' reads the medieval-dungeon dressing and drops the pressure-plate room entirely.

'A world with powers, with npcs and cool movement and in a city' names powers and NPCs but no combat, no quests and no progression, so neither 'action' nor 'rpg' is anchored in anything the user actually wrote.

Rebirth for gems, 15 unlockable zones on a currency multiplier curve, per-area pets that 'increase your clicks per second', and the literal title 'clicker phyco' make this a clicker/simulator; 'fight bosses' and 'armor' are the only rpg tokens and they sit inside an idle-upgrade economy.

'Explore the world, fight zombies and bosses' as a knight supports adventure by its verbs (explore, open landscape) and rpg by its fantasy-and-boss framing, and the prompt names no stats, loot or classes that would settle it either way.

Two penguin kingdoms fighting 'over territory' is team-vs-team combat, which is action; 'many roles to play as' means combat classes on a battlefield, not the character progression that 'rpg' implies.

The loop is 'walking around the beach' hunting shells, which is exploration/collection, but the shells are worn and procedurally unique per player, so the payoff is a personalized look - a real avatar-sim signal, not just a taxonomy artifact.

The user explicitly asks for 'adventures like spooky, fun, or even action' across a circus, a digital lake, a theme park and a void; becoming a random animal or shape is the entry premise, not a dress-up or roleplay loop.
'Try to survive in an abandoned city' states the win condition outright; playing as a cat is the avatar skin on top of it, and the prompt gives no roleplay jobs, social hub or customization.

The prompt names hunger and thirst ('you die because of other animals or not drinking or eating'), food and water scattered across a huge map, and AI predators - all survival mechanics; 'stay as that animal until death' is a permadeath rule, not roleplay.

The prompt is entirely about gun use - damage targets for money, 'use money to buy more guns', a no man's land map - and the spreadsheet has a 'shooter' bucket it chose not to use, so this is a real miss rather than a vocabulary gap.

The user says 'grand theft auto type game' (action) but the actual scope requested is 'city generation and NPCs' that 'just walk around on the sidewalks for now' with basic movement - an inhabited city with no crime or combat yet - so the stated intent and the requested content point to different labels.

Every described loop is heists, pursuit, interception and arrests with drills, C4 and jammers - 'action' fits that, whereas leading with 'simulation' elevates the loot-laundering economy over the chases and break-ins that occupy the whole document.

The feature list is split down the middle: a persistent city with houses, working traffic, a day/night cycle, a dealership and character customization argues roleplay, while pistols through sniper rifles, SWAT trucks and arrests argue action, and the prompt commits to both equally.
